Premise confirmed by tracing the code at the reviewed head (a7fb363bef6, worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):

- `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:111` calls `_resolve_assigned_reviewer(...)`, which returns exactly one user id: line 206 `acting = next((user for user in resolved if user.id == task_created_by_id), resolved[0])`, line 207 `return acting.id`. No other reviewer is ever consulted.

- The webhook re-review resolver `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (lines 144-156) repeats the same single-user check: line 151 resolves one id, line 154 returns `None` when that user's toggle is off. So later pushes also skip review while a different assignee is opted in.
- The stated contract at the reviewed head is "any assigned reviewer": PR #75215 body ("at least one of the assigned users has `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled"); toggle copy in the worktree `products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1060` `aria-label="Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs"`; and the maintainer decision recorded in `playground/stamphog-inbox-review/GRILL.md` line 57 (resolved 2026-07-28, before this head commit of 2026-07-31): "the stamphog leg fires when **any** resolved suggested reviewer has the toggle on ... Both stamphog gate call sites change together — `handle_task_run_saved` and `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`".
- Tests at the reviewed head only cover the ReviewHog toggle for the multi-assignee case (`products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:229` `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review`); every stamphog test (`lines 315-385`) uses a single assignee "alice", so the two-assignee stamphog case is untested.
- Corroboration that maintainers treated this as a defect: the shipped version of the feature (master commit abef3d7a593, PR #72680, merged 2026-07-31) replaced this with `_pick_stamphog_reviewer` in `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:170-183`, whose docstring says "Any assigned reviewer's opt-in is enough ... narrowing to one reviewer would drop reviews the other assignees asked for", with `opted_in = [user for user in resolved if settings_by_user[user.id].stamphog_review_inbox_prs]`.

Impact: a user who turned the toggle on gets no Stamphog review (initial or on later pushes) on any inbox PR where they are not the first resolved reviewer or the task creator, with no error and no workaround (the Inbox "Add reviewer" appends to the end of the list, so the user cannot make themselves canonical).
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Maybe single-acting-reviewer is the intended contract. The module docstring (receivers.py:10-18) and `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` docstring (lines 165-170) do document single-reviewer semantics, citing maintainer decisions 2026-07-02/03. But those decisions predate and concern the ReviewHog leg (which needs one person's perspectives/urgency threshold); the later decision of 2026-07-28 in GRILL.md item 1 explicitly splits the stamphog leg to "any resolved reviewer", and the PR description at this head states the same. The code's self-consistent docstring does not override the PR's stated contract and the toggle copy. (2) Maybe stamphog's side re-checks other reviewers. `products/stamphog/backend/facade/inbox_hooks.py` only stores the callable registered by review_hog; the webhook path calls that resolver, which is the same single-user function. No second check exists. (3) Maybe an existing test pins the behavior. `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` pins it for the ReviewHog toggle only; no stamphog test has two assignees. Refutation fails.

votes.evidence:
The finding's premise ("the feature must run when any assigned reviewer enables the Stamphog toggle") is contradicted by the documented, tested contract in the worktree. The design is one acting reviewer whose two per-user toggles gate both legs:

- /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:10-15 and :17-18: "The acting reviewer — whose `review_inbox_prs` gates the review ... The same resolved acting reviewer carries a second, independent toggle: `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`".
- receivers.py:166-170: acting reviewer = task creator when assigned, else the FIRST resolved reviewer "(maintainer decisions, 2026-07-02/03)"; "Their `review_inbox_prs` / `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggles gate the respective reviews".
- products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:83-87: the bot-author carve-out applies only to a PR "whose acting reviewer opted in via ReviewHog's per-user `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle. Rules that keep the exception narrow: ...". A Stamphog run posts a real GitHub approval, so the gate is deliberately per-acting-reviewer, not any-assignee.
- products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1053-1057: the toggle is per-user copy ("Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs").
- Existing tests encode exactly the behavior the finding calls a bug: products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:229-238 `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` ("if they kept the default off, a later reviewer's opt-in must not hijack"); :315-316 the parameterized toggle test states "the two toggles on the one acting reviewer gate their reviews independently"; :370-385 the webhook resolver test asserts the same single acting reviewer keyed on the stamphog toggle. The two legs use one shared `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (receivers.py:111, :151), so initial and re-review are consistent by construction, which the finding itself concedes.
votes.refutation: The finding asserts a requirement ("any assigned reviewer's opt-in must trigger Stamphog") that exists nowhere in the code, docs, UI copy, or tests; every source states the opposite: the acting reviewer (creator-if-assigned, else first resolved assignee) is the gate for both toggles, by recorded maintainer decision. Its suggestion (pick the first assignee with the toggle on) is precisely the "later reviewer's opt-in hijacks" behavior that `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` forbids for the sibling toggle, and it would widen a security-sensitive carve-out (real GitHub approvals on bot PRs) that stamphog/AGENTS.md says to keep narrow. The only true statement, that no test pins this for the Stamphog toggle specifically, is a test-coverage observation, not a defect. This is a design-preference disagreement, not a bug.

votes.evidence:
Code at the frozen head (/Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py): `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` (lines 159-207) returns exactly one user id — `next((u for u in resolved if u.id == task_created_by_id), resolved[0])` at line 206. `handle_task_run_saved` loads only that user's settings (line 114) and gates the stamphog dispatch on `settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` (line 126). `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (lines 144-156), the hook stamphog's webhook path calls for re-reviews, resolves the same single user (line 151) and returns None when that one user's toggle is off (line 154). No path consults any other assignee's toggle.

Reachability in production: `MAX_SUGGESTED_REVIEWERS = 3` (products/signals/backend/report_generation/resolve_reviewers.py:45), so reports routinely carry 2-3 assignees; the Inbox "Add reviewer" action appends to the end of the list (playground/stamphog-inbox-review/GRILL.md:58 "the Inbox 'Add' button appends to the *end*, so self-adding doesn't gate"). The stage-1 rollout population was one user self-testing his own Inbox PRs (GRILL.md:50-52, 68) — exactly the case where he is neither task creator nor resolved[0] and his opt-in is ignored. The UI copy promises per-user behavior: "Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs" (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1054, 1061), which the code does not honor for non-primary assignees.

Maintainer confirmation: the same PR was merged as #72680 (abef3d7a593) with both call sites changed to any-assignee semantics — `_pick_stamphog_reviewer` at receivers.py:173-182 on master ("Any assigned reviewer's opt-in is enough ... narrowing to one reviewer would drop reviews the other assignees asked for"), used by both `handle_task_run_saved` (line 121) and `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` (line 170). GRILL.md:57 records the decision (2026-07-28) to change exactly this, for exactly the reason the finding gives (split semantics would also make a later push dismiss an approval while someone is still opted in). The frozen head a7fb363bef6 is not an ancestor of the merge commit, i.e. it predates that fix. Existing tests (test_inbox_trigger.py:311-337, 371-388) only use a single reviewer "alice", so nothing covered the two-assignee case.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: the module docstring (receivers.py:10-19, 160-173) and GRILL.md decision 6 (2026-07-21, "Same acting reviewer, same receiver") document single-acting-reviewer gating as the intended design at the time, so one could argue this is a design choice, not a bug. That fails because (a) the user-facing toggle copy ("your Inbox PRs") promises per-user opt-in that the code silently breaks for any assignee who is not first or the task creator, (b) stamphog never reads the acting user's per-user options (it is provenance only), so there was no functional reason to narrow to one reviewer, and (c) the maintainer explicitly reversed that design a week later and changed both call sites before the PR merged. Blast radius is narrow (an opt-in feature silently does not run; no wrong approval is posted), and the fix already shipped on master, hence should_fix rather than must_fix.
